description: A microcontroller board built around the same ATmega328p chip as the Uno, in a smaller form factor, with two extra analog-only pins (A6/A7).
how_to_use: Connect it to a computer over USB to upload a sketch (program); it then runs that program on its own, reading inputs and driving outputs.

plain.what: A tiny Arduino — the same brain as the Uno in a board the size of a thumb, made to push straight into a breadboard.
plain.how: Push it across the middle gap of a breadboard, plug in a USB cable, and wire your parts to the pins next to it. The pin names are printed on the board.
